title: Flood Advisory
description: * WHAT...Coastal Flooding from abnormally high tides. * WHERE...Low-lying areas along the Sacramento River, San Joaquin River, and other Delta waterways in Solano, Yolo, Sacramento, and San Joaquin Counties. * WHEN...Until 445 PM PST Thursday. * IMPACTS...Flooding of low-lying areas including parks, lots, roads, marshes, and vulnerable islands. Erosion along levees is possible. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS... - At 1253 PM PST, NWS meteorologists have determined that abnormally high tides will result in Coastal Flooding. - The highest tides forecast each day are (all times local time): * Port Chicago: 1.0 ft above normal (5.9 ft MLLW) at 9:10 AM Wed 11/18, 1.3 ft above normal (6.2 ft MLLW) at 9:41 AM Thu 11/19, 1.6 ft above normal (6.5 ft MLLW) at 10:07 AM Fri 11/20, and 2.0 ft above normal (6.9 ft MLLW) at 10:32 AM Sat 11/21. * West Sacramento: 1.4 ft above normal (5.7 ft MLLW) at 12:09 PM Wed 11/18, 1.6 ft above normal (6.0 ft MLLW) at 12:37 PM Thu 11/19, 1.9 ft above normal (6.3 ft MLLW) at 1:04 PM Fri 11/20, and 2.3 ft above normal (6.6 ft MLLW) at 1:35 PM Sat 11/21. * Rio Vista (Datum NAVD88): +6.5 ft at 11:00 AM Wed 11/18, +6.9 ft at 12:00 PM Thu 11/19, +6.4 ft at 12:00 PM Fri 11/20, and +6.8 ft at 1:00 PM Sat 11/21. - These predictions include up to +2.1 feet of storm surge that will enhance the astronomical tide and flooding threat. Timing of high tide may vary by several hours throughout the San Francisco Bay and Delta. - Real-time water levels and latest forecasts are available at: * Port Chicago: https://tidesandcurrents.noaa.gov/noaatidepre dictions.html?id=9415144 * West Sacramento: https://tidesandcurrents.noaa.gov/noaatide predictions.html?id=9416131 * Rio Vista: https://water.noaa.gov/gauges/RVBC1

title: Flood Warning
description: * WHAT...Flooding caused by upstream dam release continues. * WHERE...Maricopa County in south central Arizona... Northeastern Yuma County in southwestern Arizona... * WHEN...Until 1100 AM MST Tuesday Nov 24. * IMPACTS...Flooding of rivers, creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations is expected. Low-water crossings are likely to become inundated with water and may not be passable. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS... - At 815 AM MST, water releases from Painted Rock Dam continue with flow peaking around 3000 cfs. A streamflow gauge immediately downstream also indicated a stage near 10 feet. - Flooding is expected along the Gila River. - Some locations that will experience flooding include... Farmlands and low-water crossings along the Gila River. - http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

title: Flood Advisory
description: * WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues. * WHERE...Southern Canovanas County in Puerto Rico... Ceiba County in Puerto Rico... Gurabo County in Puerto Rico... Juncos County in Puerto Rico... title: Flood Warning
description: ...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida... St Johns River Near Cocoa 9w affecting Brevard County. .Extreme rainfall over the headwaters of the St. Johns River has caused the river near Cocoa to rise through Major Flood Stage and has now quickly passed record flood stage. Additional heavy rainfall over the next 48 hours will continue to produce river rises above record flood levels through late week and into this weekend. For the St. Johns River...including Cocoa 9w, Above Lake Harney, Sanford, Deland, Astor...Major flooding is forecast. * WHAT...Major flooding is occurring and major flooding is forecast. The forecast river level is above the all time flood of record. * WHERE...St Johns River near Cocoa 9w. * WHEN...Until further notice. * IMPACTS...At 17.2 feet, Water enters homes along the St Johns River in the Lake Poinsett area west of Cocoa, also low lying homes in the Silver Pines subdivision in Rockledge and the Shakespeare Park area of Cocoa. Providence Road area west of Cocoa becomes impassable, cutting off access to homes in the Mullet Lane and Bass Road area. Docks flooded and water in parking lot at Lone Cabbage Fish Camp. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS... - At 1:15 PM EST Thursday the stage was 18.3 feet. - Bankfull stage is 15.8 feet. - Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending at 1:15 PM EST Thursday was 18.3 feet. - Forecast...The river is expected to remain steady above flood stage at 18.3 feet. - Flood stage is 16.0 feet. - http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

title: Flash Flood Warning
description: FFWSJU The National Weather Service in San Juan has issued a * Flash Flood Warning for... Naguabo County in Puerto Rico... * Until 600 PM AST. * At 253 PM AST, Doppler radar indicated thunderstorms producing heavy rain across the warned area. Between 2 and 3 inches of rain have fallen. Additional rainfall amounts of 1 to 2 inches are possible in the warned area. Flash flooding is ongoing or expected to begin shortly. HAZARD...Flash flooding caused by thunderstorms. SOURCE...Radar indicated. IMPACT...Flash flooding of small creeks and streams, urban areas, highways, streets and underpasses as well as other poor drainage and low-lying areas.

title: Flood Warning
description: ...Forecast flooding changed from Moderate to Major severity for the following rivers in Florida... St Johns River Near Astor affecting Volusia and Lake Counties. .On the St Johns River at Astor, the river is forecast to continue to rise through Moderate Flood Stage, reaching Major Flood Stage into early next week due to strong onshore flow causing a surge up the river as well as additional heavy rainfall expected across the basin. For the St. Johns River...including Astor...Major flooding is forecast. * WHAT...Moderate flooding is occurring and major flooding is forecast. * WHERE...St Johns River near Astor. * WHEN...Until further notice. * IMPACTS...At 4.0 feet, Major flooding occurs with water entering many structures on canals and along the river. Long duration flooding will occur, with levels taking weeks to months to return below flood stage. Water rescues will be necessary. River Road becomes inaccessible, with 1 to 2 feet water depth in numerous homes on Wildhog, Possum, Bonnet and Snail roads. Roads along Blue Creek are inaccessible with major flooding of homes on Otter, Branch and Chestnut roads. Camp South Moon Road and Juno Trail are inaccessible. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS... - At 8:30 AM EST Thursday the stage was 3.2 feet. - Bankfull stage is 2.0 feet. - Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending at 8:30 AM EST Thursday was 3.2 feet. - Forecast...The river is expected to rise to 4.0 feet Monday morning. Additional rises are possible thereafter. - Flood stage is 2.3 feet. - http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
